extracted.intended_audience: foundation program officers, nonprofit grantseekers (esp. Hispanic-serving organizations), and researchers of philanthropy
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based evaluation of U.S. private foundation policies, procedures, and grantmaking practices with emphasis on support for Hispanic needs, including transparency, applicant communications, staffing, technical assistance, and types of educational R&D supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish annual/biennial reports (transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations issuing annual and/or biennial reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes that 83% of responding foundations publish annual/biennial reports (Table 17) and compares this with a much lower national average; publishing is presented as a measure of openness and public accountability. Annual reports and similar publications increase public access to information about foundation finances and grantmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of information / mailing lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should disseminate publications and include organizations/institutions in mailing lists upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissemination increases minorities' chance of identifying relevant funders. 71.6% said they would include organizations in mailing lists; only 10.8% have a separate Hispanic mailing list. Wide dissemination is recommended to improve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to letters of inquiry (responsiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations will respond to letters of inquiry from prospective applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 97.1% of responding foundations indicated they would respond to letters of inquiry (Table 19); responsiveness is highlighted as atypically high among respondents and important for applicant access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations provide applicants with application deadlines upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 80.4% of responding foundations reported they would provide application deadlines (Table 20). Listing deadlines is treated as basic procedural information that supports applicant planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide suggestions for proposal length
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations provide guidance on recommended proposal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 74.5% said they provide suggestions for proposal length (Table 20); this is listed as a common type of procedural information foundations may offer to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide suggestions for proposal format
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations provide guidance on preferred proposal format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76.5% of responding foundations provide suggestions for proposal format (Table 20). The text emphasizes that lack of publicly available basic information on format is a common barrier for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide dates when Executive Board meets
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations provide the dates when the Executive Board meets to consider proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76.5% indicated they provide board meeting dates (Table 20); knowing meeting cycles helps applicants time submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer feedback on preliminary drafts or concept papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations provide feedback on preliminary drafts or concept papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 63.7% reported they would provide feedback on drafts (Table 20). This is presented as an atypically applicant-friendly practice among respondents and important for improving proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise on other funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations advise applicants on alternate funding sources for a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 44.1% reported providing advice on other funding sources (Table 20). Only 34% said they would advise unsuccessful applicants on alternate funding, indicating this is less commonly offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge receipt of proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations acknowledge receipt of proposals from applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 88% of responding foundations said they would acknowledge receipt; the report contrasts this positive response with common complaints that many foundations do not acknowledge proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate decisions in writing to unsuccessful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations inform unsuccessful applicants in writing when a proposal will not be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding foundations overwhelmingly expressed they would notify unsuccessful applicants in writing; 80.4% said they would explain reasons for rejection. Written notification and explanations are framed as good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain reasons for rejection to unsuccessful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations explain to unsuccessful applicants the reasons for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 80.4% of respondents indicated they would explain rejection reasons; the report highlights this as an applicant-friendly behavior not universally practiced in the foundation world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact applicants for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations contact applicants to request additional information when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 79.4% of foundations indicated they would contact applicants for additional information in response to worthy but poorly drafted proposals (Table 21). Contacting applicants is recommended as a means to salvage good ideas that were poorly presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage revision and resubmission of worthy but poorly drafted proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations encourage applicants to revise and resubmit proposals that contain good ideas but are poorly drafted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28.4% said they would encourage revision and resubmission; only 3.9% would immediately reject. The report treats encouragement and assistance as preferable practices to outright rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer technical assistance to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations offer technical assistance (TA) to strengthen applicant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical assistance is identified as limited: only 24.5% claimed to have a person providing TA. The report cites other studies noting foundations rarely invest the time to cultivate inexperienced groups, though TA is recommended to help minority groups present ideas effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have full-time administrative staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should employ full-time administrative/professional staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report stresses that without professional staff, proposals are less likely to be adequately investigated and served. 92% of respondents reported having full-time staff; staffed foundations are more likely to pursue innovative programs and provide applicant support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Hispanic-inclusive outreach and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should maintain Hispanic mailing lists or include Hispanic organizations in general lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 10.8% of responding foundations reported having a Hispanic mailing list; 6.8% include Hispanics in a general list but not a separate list. The report highlights the scarcity of targeted outreach as a barrier to Hispanic applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Hispanics on boards, staff, or as consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should appoint Hispanics as full-time employees, trustees, or consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey found 12 foundations claimed full-time Hispanic employees and 13 Hispanic board members across 12 foundations; overall representation is low (1.9% of employees). The report connects board/staff composition with foundation sensitivity to minority needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt affirmative hiring/promotion policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should develop formal affirmative action policies for hiring and promotion of minority staff and trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing prior surveys, the report notes very few foundations had written affirmative action policies; the presence of such policies is presented as a way to improve minority employment and trustee representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Educational Research & Development (R&D) activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should support educational R&D activities relevant to Hispanic communities (internships, fellowships, conferences, surveys, community needs assessments, research, publications, workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The questionnaire listed activities comprising Educational R&D; support was low across items (Table 23). Examples with percentages: internships 20.6%, graduate fellowships 15.7%, ongoing research by organizations 17.6%, publication of results 6.9%. The report treats support for such activities as critical but limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide program and application publications (brochures, guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should issue brochures, application guidelines, and other publications describing policies, grants, and application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 39 foundations (38%) issue two or more publications; many foundations provide procedural information on request. The report cites lack of basic information availability as a barrier to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise applicants to study guidelines and adhere to them
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised to study foundation guidelines and adhere to them when applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 22 records suggestions foundations gave to minority applicants; 20 foundations suggested studying and adhering to guidelines. This is presented as a common foundation expectation for successful applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants should improve proposal content and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must improve the quality of proposal contents and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 17 foundations recommended improving proposal quality (Table 22). The report emphasizes that good ideas often fail because proposals are not well written, especially among groups lacking proposal-writing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants should improve management, budgeting, and fundraising capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate adequate management, budgeting, and fund-raising capacity in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 14 foundations recommended strengthening organizational management and financial planning as part of improving funding prospects (Table 22). Foundations cite organizational capacity as an important evaluative factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants should research target foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should conduct research on target foundations to align proposals with funder priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 14 foundations recommended that applicants research target foundations (Table 22). The report suggests matching proposals to foundation interests increases likelihood of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants should request technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to request technical assistance from foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 7 foundations explicitly suggested requesting TA (Table 22), yet the report notes TA availability is limited; applicants are advised to seek TA where available to improve proposal competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspectability of private foundation tax returns (public access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private foundations must permit inspection of tax returns by the public; tax returns are available at the Foundation Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes tax returns are publicly available and that limited voluntary annual reporting by foundations makes tax returns a key transparency source. This is presented as a procedural/legal expectation rather than an evaluative criterion for proposals.
